title: C# syntax — quick overview
rememberThis: C# has no Automatic Semicolon Insertion (ASI); every statement ends with a semicolon or uses a block.
if ( ) requires a bool — C# will not treat 0 or "" as false like JavaScript.
Classic switch does not fall through; you need break, return, throw, or goto case.
foreach walks a sequence; for is for when you need an index.
C# 11 raw strings (""" ... """) and C# 14 null-conditional assignment (x?.Prop = value) and nameof(List<>).
#if removes code at compile time; #nullable toggles static analysis (full Nullable Reference Type rules in module 07).
bullets: Integer division truncates toward zero; use decimal (m suffix) for money.
?? supplies a fallback when null; ?. skips access when the receiver is null.
C# 14: x?.Prop = expr assigns only when x is not null; the right-hand side is skipped otherwise.
checked makes integer overflow throw OverflowException; default context wraps silently.
sizeof works on unmanaged value types only — not classes or strings on the heap.
break exits the nearest loop or switch; continue skips to the next iteration.
